external_entities.name: shopper
external_entities.description: A person who browses the storefront, signs in, and places orders.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Shoppers browse the storefront and place orders

external_entities.name: card processor
external_entities.description: A third-party payment processor that settles payments and sends payment webhooks.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our card processor is a third party.

processes.name: storefront API
processes.description: A Node service running on Cloud Run that serves storefront interactions and receives payment webhooks.
processes.source_excerpt: the storefront API, a Node service running on Cloud Run

processes.name: order service
processes.description: A Python worker that processes orders, accesses the orders database, and writes receipts.
processes.source_excerpt: The order service is a Python worker in our core network

data_stores.name: orders-db
data_stores.description: A PostgreSQL database containing orders, shopper addresses, and card-last-four data.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Orders, shopper addresses and card-last-four live in a PostgreSQL database (orders-db)

data_stores.name: receipt archive
data_stores.description: A Cloud Storage bucket containing receipts for completed orders.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Every completed order also gets a receipt written to a Cloud Storage bucket we call the receipt archive.

data_flows.name: browse storefront
data_flows.description: The shopper browses the storefront through the storefront API.

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: The shopper signs in using an email and password and receives a session cookie.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Shoppers sign in with email and password and get a session cookie
data_flows.notes: MFA has not been rolled out for shopper accounts.

data_flows.name: place orders
data_flows.description: The shopper places orders through the storefront API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: place orders through the storefront API

data_flows.name: submit order
data_flows.description: The storefront API calls the order service over gRPC when a shopper submits an order.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When a shopper submits an order the storefront API calls the order service over gRPC.

data_flows.name: read and write orders
data_flows.description: The order service reads and writes orders data in the orders database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the order service reads and writes with a single application account that has full read/write
data_flows.authentication: single application account; password from an environment variable on the worker

data_flows.name: write receipt
data_flows.description: The order service writes a receipt for every completed order to the receipt archive.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every completed order also gets a receipt written to a Cloud Storage bucket we call the receipt archive.
data_flows.data_description: receipt records which order was written and that the order service wrote it

data_flows.name: settlement webhook
data_flows.description: The card processor posts a webhook to the storefront API after settling a payment.
data_flows.source_excerpt: After they settle a payment they POST a webhook back to the storefront API to tell us the order is paid.
data_flows.notes: The source states: "I would have to check how that callback is authenticated."
data_flows.data_description: notification that the order is paid

trust_boundaries.name: core network
trust_boundaries.description: The core network in which the order service runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The order service is a Python worker in our core network

assumptions.assumption: The storefront API presents a web interface because shoppers browse the storefront and place orders through it.
assumptions.basis: The source describes the storefront API as the interface used by shoppers to browse the storefront and place orders.

assumptions.assumption: The order service presents a non-web interface because it is reached through gRPC, which is an RPC service interface rather than a web application interface.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the storefront API calls the order service over gRPC.

assumptions.assumption: The orders database contains confidential data because it stores shopper addresses and card-last-four data alongside orders.
assumptions.basis: The source states that orders, shopper addresses, and card-last-four live in orders-db.
